basis.note: Anchored on the Cambridge Markov Chains schedule (read through an extraction), with the Poisson process and the M/M/1 queue from Applied Probability. Renewal theory, general continuous-time chains, martingales and Brownian motion are not built.

big_ideas.title: Condition on the first step
big_ideas.text: Hitting probabilities, expected times and invariant distributions all come from one move of the chain and a set of linear equations.

big_ideas.title: Equilibrium is a balance of flows
big_ideas.text: A distribution is invariant when probability flowing into each state equals what flows out; detailed balance is the special case where it balances pair by pair.

practices.title: Compute
practices.text: Carry the definition or theorem to a number, a count or an example.

practices.title: Decide
practices.text: Say whether a statement holds, which hypothesis fails, or which example breaks it.

los.do: Compute n-step transition probabilities and push a distribution forward one step.
ek: The n-step probabilities are the entries of Pⁿ (Chapman-Kolmogorov), and a row vector of probabilities evolves by μ ↦ μP.

los.do: Find the communicating classes of a chain, say which are closed, and find the period of a state.
ek: States communicate when each can reach the other. A class is closed if the chain cannot leave it; a chain with one class is irreducible. The period of a state is the gcd of its possible return times.

los.do: Find an absorption probability and a mean hitting time by first-step analysis.
ek: h(i), the probability of hitting A from i, satisfies h = 1 on A and h(i) = Σ p(i, j) h(j) elsewhere. k(i), the mean time to hit A, satisfies k = 0 on A and k(i) = 1 + Σ p(i, j) k(j).

los.do: Solve the gambler's ruin problem for the chance of winning and the expected duration.
ek: On 0…N with up-probability p and q = 1 − p: from i the chance of reaching N first is i/N if p = 1/2 and (1 − (q/p)^i)/(1 − (q/p)^N) otherwise. The fair game lasts i(N − i) steps on average.

los.do: Say whether a random walk is recurrent or transient and find a biased walk's return probability.
ek: A state is recurrent if return is certain, equivalently if Σ pⁿ(i, i) diverges. The simple symmetric walk is recurrent in one and two dimensions and transient in three (Pólya). On the integers with p ≠ 1/2 the return probability is 1 − |p − q|.

los.do: Find the invariant distribution of a small chain.
ek: π is invariant when πP = π with entries summing to 1. For two states with p(0, 1) = a and p(1, 0) = b, π = (b, a)/(a + b).

los.do: Relate the invariant distribution to mean return times and long-run proportions.
ek: In an irreducible positive-recurrent chain the mean return time to i is 1/π_i, and the long-run proportion of time spent in i is π_i whatever the start.

los.do: Use detailed balance, including for a random walk on a graph.
ek: If π_i p(i, j) = π_j p(j, i) for all pairs then π is invariant and the chain is reversible. A random walk on a graph has π_v = deg(v)/(2E).

los.do: Say when a chain converges to equilibrium and how fast.
ek: An irreducible aperiodic positive-recurrent chain has pⁿ(i, j) → π_j. For two states, pⁿ(0, 0) − π₀ = π₁ λⁿ with λ = 1 − a − b, the second eigenvalue.

los.do: Compute probabilities and waiting times for a Poisson process.
ek: With rate λ, the number of arrivals in time t is Poisson with mean λt, the gaps are independent exponentials of mean 1/λ, and the kth arrival comes at mean time k/λ.

Independent Poisson processes of rates λ and μ superpose to rate λ + μ, and the next event is from the first with probability λ/(λ + μ). Keeping each event with probability p gives a Poisson process of rate pλ.

los.do: Find the equilibrium of a birth-death chain and of the M/M/1 queue.
ek: Balance across each cut: π_n λ_n = π_(n+1) μ_(n+1). For M/M/1 with ρ = λ/μ < 1, π_n = (1 − ρ)ρⁿ and the mean number in the system is ρ/(1 − ρ).
